body.x: Vspace (CEO David Seungwon Paek) will participate in CES 2025 from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas at the K-Startup Pavilion. The company specializes in manufacturing UAM (Urban Air Mobility) aircraft equipped with high-density batteries, achieving a high maximum takeoff weight (MTOW) relative to the payload. Vspace's electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft are designed to support last-mile mobility solutions for goods and passengers, positioning the company as a leader in sustainable urban air mobility solutions. Their flagship models include the VS-300 and VS-200.

Vspace has achieved significant milestones, including delivering battery systems for refrigerated trucks to GS Global and collaborating with Hanwha Systems to develop intelligent onboard software platforms for UAM operations. The company also invests in joint R&D with U.S.-based aircraft manufacturer TAF for UAM aircraft development.

Vspace secured term sheets from U.S. investors, aiming for a valuation of KRW 70 billion by 2025. The company is in advanced discussions with Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Defense for eVTOL exports, pending strategic export approvals from South Korea’s government. Additionally, Vspace signed an agreement with UAE’s EDGE for eVTOL exports across the Middle East. The company showcased its capabilities at the Air Taxi World Congress 2024 in London, where it conducted South Korea's first-ever demonstration flight.

The VS-300, Vspace’s highlight at CES 2025, is an eVTOL aircraft designed for urban mobility. It features a lightweight structure for enhanced maneuverability, high-energy-density batteries for eco-friendly propulsion, and advanced safety systems. The aircraft is versatile, catering to metropolitan areas’ passenger and cargo transport needs.

The VS-300 is the first eVTOL in South Korea to apply for type certification from the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, and Transport. Its design employs a fully validated structural system, boasting a battery energy density of 300Wh/kg, with the battery accounting for just 200kg of the total weight. This lightweight design allows for higher payload capacity and competitive pricing. The VS-300 supports a payload of 270kg and an MTOW of 1,050 kilograms, accommodating two passengers and one pilot.

Vspace collaborates with South Korea's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, and Transport to develop a UAM certification system. This effort aims to establish unique certification standards for UAM aircraft in South Korea, enabling the country to handle applications from global UAM companies like Joby and Archer.

In addition to the VS-300, Vspace’s VS-200 is a lightweight two-seater aircraft designed for complex urban operations. Focused on safe and efficient transportation, the company is committed to shaping the future of UAM. As part of its global expansion strategy, Vspace also plans to enter the U.S. market.
